packs.title: Citywide Discoveries
packs.promise: Explore St. Louis through river history, galleries, gardens and neighborhood gathering places.

q.s: Compare shelter and open space without depending on an animal sighting
st: At an open Zoo habitat, identify one shelter feature and one open-space feature.
Sketch how an animal could choose between them; seeing an animal is not required.
Ask what the habitat sign or Zoo source says about that species' needs.

q.s: Notice how plants manage sun or shade
st: In two open Garden plantings, find leaves with different size, texture or orientation.
Make a two-column sketch of what you can actually see.
Suggest how light or moisture might explain the contrast, labeling it as your question rather than a fact.

q.s: Compare two kinds of goods or display
st: Before setting out, use Metro Transit's current trip planner to compare a transit approach with your chosen walking or ride approach to the market. Record one practical tradeoff; buying a fare or taking a ride is optional.
During market hours, choose two different public stall displays without photographing vendors or shoppers.
Notice one material, color or arrangement clue in each.
Write how the two displays invite different kinds of browsing.

packs.title: Downtown to Riverfront
packs.promise: Follow a connected path from Union Station to public art, history and the Mississippi riverfront.

q.s: Read repeating arches from the public approach
st: Use Metro Transit's current trip planner to locate Union Station's MetroLink stop and compare its public approach with the Market Street entrance. Record one access or travel tradeoff; no fare purchase or ride is required.
From the public Market Street approach, find three repeating arches or openings on Union Station.
Sketch their rhythm without entering a business or traffic area.
Describe what that repetition does to the long station frontage.

q.s: Notice how a sculpture changes a garden edge
st: On an open Citygarden path, choose one sculpture and the planting immediately beside it.
Sketch their two outlines without touching the work.
Describe how a turn on the path changes the relationship between them.

q.s: Turn a landmark into a simple shape study
st: From a paved public Arch grounds path, trace one side of the monument's curve in a sketch.
Add the horizontal horizon line beneath it.
Move a short distance and record how the shape seems to change.
